shortDescription: The German Monday spot power contract rose on Friday as renewable output outside Germany weakened and demand in the Netherlands strengthened.

children: The German Monday spot power contract rose on Friday as renewable output outside Germany weakened and demand in the Netherlands strengthened.
The German Monday baseload contract (TRDEBD3) was at €198.50 per megawatt-hour at 0720 GMT, up 15.6% from the price traded for Friday, LSEG data showed.
The equivalent French contract (TRFRBD1) was untraded, according to LSEG data.
German wind power supply is expected to rise 6.2 gigawatts to 11.8 GW on Monday, LSEG data showed.
However, renewable supply is expected to fall in France, the Netherlands and Belgium, the data showed.
Higher residual load outside Germany limits the bearish effect from stronger wind supply, said LSEG analyst Xiulan He.
The Chooz 1 and 2 reactors in northern France had outage dates extended to October 9 due to low flow rates on the Meuse river, EDF data showed.
Some rain is expected to be limited to parts of western Europe and southern France, leaving conditions on the Rhine and Rhone rivers unlikely to improve materially, EnergyScan analysts said.
The Bugey 2 reactor on the Rhone river is also expected to have reduced output on Saturday due to environmental constraints, as France continues to grapple with extreme drought, EDF data showed.
French nuclear availability rose by two percentage points, to 73% of total capacity as the Belleville 2 reactor returned from a month-long outage.
On the forward side, the German year-ahead baseload contract (TRDEBYc1) edged up 0.1% to €130.03/MWh, the data showed.
The market remains closely linked to gas, with high volatility expected as European gas storages are empty ahead of the heating season and supply is still weak, according to a Mind Energy note.
The equivalent French contract (TRFRBYc1) was untraded with an ask price of €87.35/MWh, LSEG data showed.
The European carbon market's benchmark contract
was down 0.4% to €86.62 a metric ton.

title: German Monday price up on tighter regional renewable supply
